doc.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Arranger giving out solos
summary: Gerald says an arranger should give solos to the best players.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: As an arranger, when you were trying to decide who gets the solos — is there a certain, was that your responsibility or was that—

Yeah, well it’s your responsibility as an arranger to give the solos to the best players, to the best soloists. Because if you give it to anything less, it’s just going to, you know, it’s not going to do your arrangement any good.
That’s right. But if you’ve got two great tenor players, you know.
You really don’t have much of a problem.
They might get mad at one another.
I was going to say – is there a little competition for solo space?
That doesn’t happen but you never know a guy might say I wish I’d had that solo or something. But that’s just the way the cookie crumbles sometimes.
